newsitem.title: hong kong: HK stocks edge higher in morning after soft open.
newsitem.headline: HK stocks edge higher in morning after soft open.

text.p: Hong Kong stocks recovered from initial losses in morning trade on Thursday, following through on sharp gains notched up on Wednesday but in slow trade due to the Labour Day holiday in some regional markets, brokers said.
The Hang Seng Index added 52 points, or 0.40 percent, to 12,955 after slipping to a low of 12,845.44.
Turnover was HK$2.65 billion.
"There is some profit-taking on banks and it is quite neutral following yesterday's steep surge," said Peter Lui, institutional sales trader at NAVA SC Securities.
"But we are also seeing some bargain-hunting in properties."
"Institutions are sidelined but local investors are picking up individual property stocks," said Michael Ng, dealing director at Sassoon Securities.
Cheung Kong added HK$1.00 to HK$69.00 and Sun Hung Kai Properties rose HK$1.75 to HK$85.75.
But HSBC Holdings eased HK$0.50 to HK$195.50 after rising HK$6.00 on Wednesday.
Hang Seng Bank gained HK$0.25 to HK$87.50.
Brokers said sentiment was slightly positive due to the firm tone of the U.S. market but the Hang Seng Index was expected to remain below the 13,000 level.
Wharf Holdings eased HK$0.70 to HK$28.60.
The company said it intended to contest a US$125.5 million Denver federal district court judgement against it.
"This judgement would greatly undermine the earnings of Wharf," said Sean Li, associate director at Amsteel Securities.
Shares in toy maker Kin Yat debuted at HK$2.20 on Thursday before the stock retreated to HK$1.69 at mid-morning.
The company offered 85 million shares at HK$1.28 each in an initial public offering in Hong Kong.
Shares in Lam Soon Food fell HK$0.19, or 23 percent, to HK$0.63.
The company said it planned to raise between HK$671 million and HK$689 million through a three-for-one-rights issue.
Brokers said investors remained cautious on H-shares since most of the results announced by the mainland Chinese companies were negative.
The Hang Seng Chinese Enterprises Index, or H-share index, added 2.78 points to 1,070.23.
Hang Seng Index futures May and June contracts advanced 90 points each to 12,910 and 12,940 in late morning trade.
